subject: TeleMed: request for short-lived conversational shard TTL and SIG evidence timeline
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex@telemed.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Retention ask: conversational 'shard' logs (SIG evidence & timing)

Ethan —

Thanks for taking this. Quick background: we're integrating Redwood for live clinician–patient chat; TeleMed's security team wants a narrow exception that conversational 'shard' artifacts (transient per-session slices used for routing/debug) be retained for 7 days instead of the platform default 30 days. The ask is narrow: not full message transcripts, just shard metadata and short-lived routing traces needed for triage.

SIG/CAIQ items they flagged: evidence for how the override is implemented (tenant-level TTL override), sample redacted export for compliance review, and a timeline for when we can provide artifacts (we're on a renewal in two weeks).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- create a tenant-scoped TTL override limited to 'conversation_shard' objects
- provide a sampled CSV showing redacted shard records and timestamps
- produce a short write-up for SIG section items (retention policy + proof of deletion workflow)

Appreciate a quick read on feasibility and rough ETA. Also looping in TeleMed Legal: legal@telemed.ai for docs/contract amendment implications.

—Alex
Alex Nguyen
Head of Integrations, TeleMed.AI
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@telemed.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention ask: conversational 'shard' logs (SIG evidence & timing)

Alex — thanks for the clear note and flagging Legal. We can support a narrow, tenant-scoped TTL override for specific internal object types, but need to double-check a couple of implementation and evidence details before we commit to a delivery date: 

1) Confirm object taxonomy: is 'conversation_shard' the canonical name you use, or do you mean 'session_routing_shard' / 'conversation_segment'? We need the exact object key so our infra team can scope the TTL rule.

2) Evidence scope: for SIG/CAIQ we'll provide: a) a brief architecture note describing the override (how tenant tags map to TTL enforcement), b) redacted sample export (CSV) limited to shard IDs, creation ts, TTL tag, and redaction proof, and c) a script/log snippet showing deletion job runs. Will that satisfy TeleMed Security?

3) Timeline: assuming the object key is confirmed today, we can produce a redacted sample + architecture note within 48 business hours. Full deletion proof (log snippets and retention job metadata) will take up to 5 business days. If you need these embedded into a contract amendment, loop in your legal and we can prepare a short addendum.

I'll start an internal ask to Ops and Compliance (cc'd). In the meantime, can you confirm the exact object name and whether TeleMed expects seismic-level audit (full per-token trace) or metadata-level proof?

Best,
Ethan Park
Principal, Platform Security & Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: TeleMed shard TTL exception — quick ops/compliance check

Folks — TeleMed (HS-100728) asked for a tenant-level TTL override to retain 'conversation_shard' artifacts for 7 days instead of our 30-day default. They want SIG/CAIQ evidence and a redacted sample export for their security review.

Questions:
- Marissa: can Dedicated/DynInfra create a per-tenant TTL rule scoped to a storage key class without wider exposure? Any risks to indexing/analytics pipelines?
- Neha: compliance — will a CSV of redacted shard rows + a deletion-job log snippet satisfy SIG section requests for retention proof? Or do they also expect a screenshot of retention rules in our console + signed statement?

Proposed timeline (if object name confirmed today): sample + write-up in 48 business hours, deletion-job evidence in 5 business days.

Thanks — want to be conservative on the ETA before I confirm to Alex.

—Ethan
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@telemed.ai>, TeleMed Legal <legal@telemed.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention ask: conversational 'shard' logs (SIG evidence & timing)

Alex — thanks for confirming the object name as 'conversation_shard' earlier today. We've scoped this internally and can proceed with the narrow exception as requested. Summary and deliverables below: 

What we can provide
- Tenant-scoped TTL override: Redwood will add a TTL override rule that applies only to TeleMed.AI's tenant tag and only to the storage class labeled 'conversation_shard'. This rule will set TTL = 7 days from creation timestamp. The override does not change default retention for other object classes.
- Redacted sample export: attached CSV (telemed_log-sample-20270510.csv) containing redacted shard_id, created_at, tenant_tag, ttl_tag. PII fields removed.
- SIG/CAIQ write-up: attached PDF (SIG-Evidence-section4-7.pdf) with a short architecture diagram, how TTL enforcement works, deletion-job signatures, and links to where the retention rule appears in the Console UI.
- Deletion job evidence: within 5 business days we will provide log snippets and job run metadata proving the background cleaner executed against TeleMed's tenant id with the 7-day window.

Scope and constraints
- We are not exporting full conversation transcripts as part of this deliverable. The exported fields are metadata-only.
- The tenant override will be visible to TeleMed if they have Console admin privileges; we will also provide a signed attestation that the rule was applied on the date indicated.
- Contract amendment: if TeleMed requires an SLA or permanent change to the default retention in the contract, please sign the attached amendment (DocuSign link in related links) and we'll convert the temporary exception into a contractual clause.

Next steps
1) Alex — confirm acceptance of metadata-only scope so we can start producing the artifacts.
2) TeleMed Legal — if you want the attestation wording, tell us whether you need company notarization vs standard electronic signature.

Attachments: SIG-Evidence-section4-7.pdf (write-up), telemed_log-sample-20270510.csv (redacted sample).
